question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact signed?
solution:
The correct answer is __1931__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gandhi-Irwin Pact/Delhi Pact (5th March 1931):

 
 
• Moderate statesmen Tejbahadur Sapru and Jayakar initiated efforts to bring about a rapprochement between Mahatma Gandhi and the government.
 
• Six meetings with Viceroy Lord Irwin finally led to the signing of a pact between the two to join the Second Round Table Conference.
 
• Regarding Gandhi- Irwin Pact, Jawahar Lal Nehru remarked, ‘*This is the way the world ends, not with a bang but a whimper*.
 
• It was signed before the Second Round Table Conference in London.
 
• It marked the end of the Civil Disobedience Movement in India against the British rule that Gandhi and his followers had initiated with the Salt March.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Lord Irwin (1926 AD-1931 AD):

 
 
• Simon Commission visited India in 1928.
 
• Nehru Report, 1928.
 
• Lahore Session of the Congress, (1929) and Poorna Swaraj, declaration.
 
• Civil Disobedience Movement, 1930 started.
 
• Dandi March (12 March 1930).
 
• Gandhi-Irwin Pact, 5 March 1931.
 
• Sharda Act, 1929, under which the marriageable age of girls (14 years) and boys (18 years) was raised.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose founded the Independence of India League.
